hits.original:

hits.draft_en:
OpenAI Devs: connect several machines to the same dot and let one build and test while you keep coding on your laptop.

This is the pattern I want everywhere.

Computer-use agents should not fight me for the mouse. Give them their own box, let them grind, and let me keep my laptop.

Shared desktop agents are a demo. Dedicated machines are a workflow.
hits.video_tip: Vertical 12s: your cursor and an agent's cursor fight over the same window, then a second screen lights up and the agent moves over there. Caption: 'Get your own computer'.

hits.name: OpenAI
hits.hook: OpenAI: Control Room, one system to track research workloads and halt model output within 35 seconds
hits.text:
We built Control Room, a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.

It connects every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. This works together with our misalignment monitoring systems, and halts model output within 35 seconds of a decision to intervene to stop or pause a job.

Control Room is just one part of our holistic approach for safe frontier model training and deployment.

https://t.co/tc0lBqFdS5

hits.draft_en:
OpenAI built Control Room: one place to see every research workload and halt model output within 35 seconds of deciding to intervene.

Now ask your tenant the same question.

If a Copilot Studio agent starts misbehaving at 4:55 on a Friday, how long until someone can stop it? Does anyone even know it exists?

Inventory. Owner. Off switch. Not glamorous. Very necessary.
hits.video_tip: Talking head 15s with a 35-second timer in the corner; when it hits zero, cut to a blank 'Owner' column in an agent inventory. Caption: 'What is your stop time?'

hits.draft_en:
Simon Willison found a gem in the Fable 5.2 prompting guide: tell it "This codebase is yours" and it gets less timid about improving existing code.

Very tempting to try "This solution is yours" on a Copilot Studio agent.

Then I remember who gets the Teams ping when it refactors a Dataverse table.

Give the agent ownership of the code. Keep ownership of production.
hits.video_tip: Screen 15s: type 'This codebase is yours' into a Copilot chat, the diff gets bigger and bolder, then cut to a phone buzzing with a 'Who changed the table?' Teams message. Caption: 'Ownership has limits'.

My harness post hit 7.8K views yesterday, so here is round two.

New model day is the perfect experiment. Fable 5.2 is GA in GitHub Copilot and Foundry.

Same agent, same tasks, swap the model. Then keep the model and swap the harness.

My bet: the harness moves the needle more than the model does. Prove me wrong.

🚨 Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are absolutely INSANE.

Anthropic just released its new flagship models, and the benchmarks are only half the story.

I went through the release details. Here are the 12 most interesting findings:

1. Coding benchmarks

Fable 5.2 is beating some

OpenAI kept the biggest numbers: 'Tomorrow.' teaser grew to 2.37M, connecting multiple local computers to one dot hit 1.26M, Control Room (halt model output within 35 seconds) 796K, and the Codex ModRetro Chromatic handheld 623K
safety and control is still a top-tier topic: Control Room is the second announcement in two weeks about stopping models fast, after last week's cyber posts
Simon Willison had three stars in 48 hours (219K, 151K, 41K), each one concrete: a prompt tip, a PR trick and a funny two-option poll
Microsoft corporate stayed case study and partner: Northern Trust onboarding grew to 26K, Mercedes-AMG F1 to 63K, Azure at KubeCon 6K; MSFTCopilot just cleared 5K with Copilot in Word drafts
quiet accounts: MicrosoftAI, satyanadella, clamanna, pierceboggan, sama, OpenAINewsroom and ChatGPT had no original over 5K in 48h; Mustafa Suleyman's MAI-Transcribe-2 post is brand new (1.8K so far)

drafts.rides: @simonw "This codebase is yours" (219,169) + Fable 5.2 GA in GitHub Copilot (@github 54,915, @msdev 27,724, @code 22,565)
drafts.text:
Simon Willison found a gem in the Fable 5.2 prompting guide: tell it "This codebase is yours" and it gets less timid about improving existing code.

Very tempting to try "This solution is yours" on a Copilot Studio agent.

Then I remember who gets the Teams ping when it refactors a Dataverse table.

Give the agent ownership of the code. Keep ownership of production.
drafts.video_tip: Screen 15s: type 'This codebase is yours' into a Copilot chat, the diff gets bigger and bolder, then cut to a phone buzzing with a 'Who changed the table?' Teams message. Caption: 'Ownership has limits'.

drafts.text:
OpenAI built Control Room: one place to see every research workload and halt model output within 35 seconds of deciding to intervene.

Now ask your tenant the same question.

If a Copilot Studio agent starts misbehaving at 4:55 on a Friday, how long until someone can stop it? Does anyone even know it exists?

Inventory. Owner. Off switch. Not glamorous. Very necessary.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head 15s with a 35-second timer in the corner; when it hits zero, cut to a blank 'Owner' column in an agent inventory. Caption: 'What is your stop time?'

drafts.rides: your harness post (7,797, your best this week) + Fable 5.2 GA day
drafts.text:
My harness post hit 7.8K views yesterday, so here is round two.

New model day is the perfect experiment. Fable 5.2 is GA in GitHub Copilot and Foundry.

Same agent, same tasks, swap the model. Then keep the model and swap the harness.

My bet: the harness moves the needle more than the model does. Prove me wrong.
drafts.video_tip: Split screen 20s: left side swaps the model dropdown and the score barely moves, right side swaps the harness and the score jumps. Caption: 'Model vs harness'.

drafts.text:
OpenAI Devs: connect several machines to the same dot and let one build and test while you keep coding on your laptop.

This is the pattern I want everywhere.

Computer-use agents should not fight me for the mouse. Give them their own box, let them grind, and let me keep my laptop.

Shared desktop agents are a demo. Dedicated machines are a workflow.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 12s: your cursor and an agent's cursor fight over the same window, then a second screen lights up and the agent moves over there. Caption: 'Get your own computer'.

drafts.text:
Somewhere in your environment there is a Power Automate flow that fails every third Tuesday. Do you:

1. Open run history methodically until you find it

2. Hand Copilot 400 run logs and let it triangulate

Be honest.
drafts.video_tip: Screen 10s: scroll a long wall of failed runs, freeze, then show a Copilot pane highlighting one red run. Caption: '1 or 2?'. Add an X poll with both options.
